question: Are soccer referees more likely to give red cards to dark-skin-toned players than to light-skin-toned players?
estimand: Odds ratio of a red card per game (per referee-player dyad game exposure), comparing dark-skin-toned to light-skin-toned players, estimated from the dyad-level data with rater skin tone as the exposure and redCards as the outcome.

decision_rule.metric: odds ratio of a red card per game, dark vs light skin tone

columns.name: games
columns.note: number of games the player and this referee shared (one row per player-referee dyad); it is not the player's total games

columns.name: redCards
columns.note: number of red cards the referee gave this player across their shared games

columns.name: yellowCards
columns.note: number of yellow cards the referee gave this player across their shared games

columns.name: yellowReds
columns.note: number of second yellow cards (leading to a red) the referee gave this player across their shared games

columns.name: rater1
columns.note: skin tone of the player rated by rater 1 from the photo, 0 very light to 1 very dark

columns.name: rater2
columns.note: skin tone of the player rated by rater 2 from the photo, 0 very light to 1 very dark

columns.name: leagueCountry
columns.note: country of the league the player plays in

columns.name: meanIAT
columns.note: mean implicit-bias (race IAT) score of the referee's country of origin

columns.name: meanExp
columns.note: mean explicit-bias score of the referee's country of origin

steps.title: Handle players without skin-tone ratings
steps.description: Skin tone is only available for players who were rated from photos; the choice is whether to keep only rated rows (required for the exposure) and whether to additionally require the other covariates used later.

options.label: Keep rows with both rater scores
options.rationale: Rows with a missing exposure cannot enter the comparison; this is the minimal requirement.
options.spec: Drop rows where rater1 or rater2 is missing (use the rows where both rater1 and rater2 are non-null). Create no new columns and write nothing to ctx. Return the filtered data frame.

steps.title: Construct the skin-tone exposure
steps.description: Build a binary dark-vs-light exposure from the two raters' scores; the cut-off and rater combination are alternatives.

options.label: Average of raters, split at median
options.rationale: Uses both raters and a data-driven split, common in this literature.
options.spec: Compute skin_mean = (rater1 + rater2) / 2 per row. Compute the median of skin_mean over rows that have it. Set dark_skin = 1 where skin_mean is strictly greater than that median, else 0; write the median to ctx['skin_cut'] as a number. Return the data frame.

options.label: Average of raters, split at scale midpoint
options.rationale: A fixed cut at the middle of the 0 to 1 scale avoids a data-dependent threshold.
options.spec: Compute skin_mean = (rater1 + rater2) / 2 per row. Set dark_skin = 1 where skin_mean is strictly greater than 0.5, else 0 (rows with missing skin_mean stay missing). Write 0.5 to ctx['skin_cut']. Return the data frame.

steps.title: Treatment of extreme referee-country bias scores and extreme games
steps.description: meanIAT, meanExp and games have extreme values; whether to keep them, trim the referee-country score or cap exposure days is a visible choice.

options.label: Keep all rows
options.rationale: Extreme values are genuine observations in these columns; no trimming.
options.spec: Do not remove any rows. Create no new columns and write nothing to ctx. Return the data frame unchanged.

steps.title: Choose covariates for adjustment
steps.description: Alternative covariate sets; each writes the list of column names used by the model step.

options.label: Position, league and referee country
options.rationale: Adjusts for player role and league context that plausibly relate to card rates.
options.spec: Write ctx['covariates'] = ['position', 'leagueCountry', 'refCountry']. Do not add or drop columns. Return the data frame. The model encodes these categorical columns with drop_first=True.

options.label: Minimal set plus height, weight, games and referee-country bias scores
options.rationale: Adds physical and exposure controls plus country-level implicit and explicit bias, which may confound skin tone with referee attitudes.
options.spec: Write ctx['covariates'] = ['position', 'leagueCountry', 'refCountry', 'height', 'weight', 'games', 'meanIAT', 'meanExp']. Do not add or drop columns. Return the data frame. The model encodes categorical columns with drop_first=True. (minimal: Write ctx['covariates'] = ['position', 'leagueCountry', 'refCountry']. Do not add or drop columns. Return the data frame. The model encodes these categorical columns with drop_first=True.)
options.source: Standard observational confounder adjustment; Gelman & Hill style covariate selection for pre-exposure confounders.

steps.title: Estimate the odds ratio of a red card by skin tone
steps.description: Alternative logistic estimators of the odds ratio of a red card for dark vs light skin tone, using the covariates in ctx['covariates']; the outcome is recorded as any red card or as a count per game.

options.label: Logistic regression on any red card, cluster-robust errors by player
options.rationale: Matches the stated odds-ratio metric directly by modelling whether a dyad produced any red card; clustering by player accounts for repeated rows.
options.spec: Create any_red = 1 where redCards is greater than 0, else 0. Fit statsmodels Logit with outcome any_red, regressors dark_skin plus the columns in ctx['covariates'] (categorical ones encoded with drop_first=True) and an intercept, using cov_type='cluster' with groups = playerShort codes. Estimate = exp(coefficient of dark_skin); ci_low and ci_high = exp of the 95% Wald interval bounds; p_value = two-sided p for dark_skin. Return these four numbers.

options.label: Logistic regression on any red card, heteroskedasticity-robust errors
options.rationale: Gives the same odds-ratio scale with ordinary robust errors, a check on whether clustering by player changes the interval.
options.spec: Create any_red = 1 where redCards is greater than 0, else 0. Fit statsmodels Logit with outcome any_red, regressors dark_skin plus the columns in ctx['covariates'] (categorical ones encoded with drop_first=True) and an intercept, using cov_type='HC1'. Estimate = exp(coefficient of dark_skin); ci_low and ci_high = exp of the 95% Wald interval bounds; p_value = two-sided p for dark_skin. Return these four numbers.
options.source: Cameron & Miller (2015), A Practitioner's Guide to Cluster-Robust Inference, J. Human Resources
